=== History ===
The date of establishment is uncertain<ref>Kawabashi Zengorō, “Tōto Seto: Commemorative Publication of the Enforcement of the City System,” Wada Chūji, 1930, pp. 102–103</ref>. During the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, it was called '''Hachioji''' and served as the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} (guardian deity) of Akazu Village. Behind the shrine buildings is a {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|simple|Round Kofun|zh|圓墳|qid=Q11394747}} called the “Ōma Shrine Kofun,” constructed in the {{ill|7th century|Q8089|qid=Q8089}}. The {{ill|Shinkan (official)|Q11589454|qid=Q11589454}} traditionally bore the name “Nakajima Zendaifu,” and records from the {{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} era are said to exist, though the lineage has since died out. Ridge tags (munafuda) relating to the main hall from 1653 (Jōō 2) and 1805 (Bunka 2) have been confirmed<ref name="AichiPrefecture"/>.

In 1840 (Tenpō 11), an old manuscript scroll of the {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|Q11041830|qid=Q11041830}} inscribed “Ōma Hachioji-gū” was discovered, and what appears to be a prayer talisman bore the inscription “Ōma Hachioji Daimyōjin”<ref name="AichiPrefecture"/>. The location was also known as Ōmamori<ref name="AichiPrefecture"/>.  
Based on these sources, it came to be identified with the “Ōma Shrine” of Yamada District in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, and this has become the established theory<ref name="AichiPrefecture"/>. Prior to this, there were various theories regarding the shrine’s location, including one identifying it with Dainichidō in Nishisugi Village and another with Ōdome Village, which had a similar name.

=== Cultural Properties ===
=== City-Designated Cultural Properties ===
* Stone Torii Gate<ref name="DesignatedRegisteredCulturalPropertiesList">[https://www.city.seto.aichi.jp/docs/2010/11/10/01189/index.html List of Designated and Registered Cultural Properties] Seto City</ref>  
** Completed in 1755 (Hōreki 5)<ref name="ChunichiShimbun19960214">“Stone Torii of Ōma Shrine and Oribe Lantern of Fukagawa Shrine Designated as Seto City Cultural Properties,” Chunichi Shimbun, February 14, 1996</ref>. Designated as a Seto City Cultural Property on February 9, 1996 (Heisei 8)<ref name="DesignatedRegisteredCulturalPropertiesList"/>. The stone torii of Hachiman Shrine in Yawata-chō, Seto City, is also designated as a Seto City Cultural Property<ref name="DesignatedRegisteredCulturalPropertiesList"/>.  
** Height: 3.87 meters<ref name="ChunichiShimbun19960214"/>. A {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Myōjin torii}}<ref name="ChunichiShimbun19960214"/>. The kasagi (top lintel) is double-layered and has a curved shape<ref name="ChunichiShimbun19960214"/>. It is a stone torii from a period when wooden torii were more common<ref name="ChunichiShimbun19960214"/>.  

=== Registered Tangible Cultural Property ===
* Main Hall  
** Completed in 1805 (Bunka 2)<ref name="CulturalHeritageOnline"/><ref name="AichiPrefecture">[https://www.city.seto.aichi.jp/docs/2023/05/29/R6/oomajinnjahonnden.pdf Ōma Shrine Main Hall] Aichi Prefecture</ref>. Renovated in 1977 (Shōwa 52)<ref name="AichiPrefecture"/>. Registered as a {{ill|Registered Tangible Cultural Property of Japan|Q11579194|qid=Q11579194}} on March 6, 2024 (Reiwa 6)<ref name="CulturalHeritageOnline"/>. The registration criterion is “items that serve as a model for design”<ref name="AichiPrefecture"/>.  
** Three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} style, copper-sheet roofing, single-story structure<ref name="CulturalHeritageOnline"/>. Building area: 12 m²<ref name="CulturalHeritageOnline"/>. A veranda with gibōshi balustrades runs around three sides<ref name="CulturalHeritageOnline"/>.
